intro: Every category sells a little differently. A serum buyer wants to see texture, a sneaker buyer checks the sole, and a coffee buyer wants to watch the pour. These pages sort ideas by what you sell, so you can start with the shots that answer your shoppers' real questions instead of guessing. Each one covers the photos and short videos worth making first, the details to get right in your upload, and questions other sellers in that category often ask.

Start on the page for your main product, even if your catalog spans several categories. The examples there are matched to how people shop for that item: close texture shots for beauty, fit and fabric shots for clothing, scale and setting shots for home goods. You can open the photo or video tool from each example and reuse the same product photo across every look.

features.d: Each page names the photos and short videos sellers in that category make first, so you start with the shot that answers a real shopper question.
See what has to stay visible for your item, such as the full label on a bottle, the sole on a shoe, or the finish on a piece of jewelry.
Reuse one product photo across white background shots, lifestyle scenes and vertical videos without a reshoot.
Pick real ad types such as unboxing, demo, review and limited-time offer instead of browsing generic room settings.
Every example links to the tool and ready-made template that produced it, so the page ends in an asset you can download.

faq.q: Which industry page should I use for a mixed catalog?
faq.a: Start with the page that matches your main product, then borrow scene ideas from the other relevant category. The same photo and video tools work across categories.

faq.q: My category isn't listed. Can I still use AIVideosUGC?
faq.a: Yes. The tools aren't limited to these categories. Pet supplies, toys, stationery, and outdoor gear sellers can make white background photos, lifestyle scenes, and short video ads the same way.

faq.q: Can I use a phone photo to get started?
faq.a: Yes. Use a sharp, evenly lit phone photo with the whole product in frame; professional equipment is not required. Upload only a photo you own or have permission to use.

faq.q: What's the difference between the industry pages and the templates?
faq.a: The industry pages explain what to shoot for your product and why shoppers need it; templates apply a chosen look to the photo you upload. Open an industry page to plan the shot, then pick a linked template to produce it.

faq.q: Can one product photo be used for both photos and videos?
faq.a: Yes. A clear square photo with the whole product visible can produce white background and lifestyle photos, and it also works as the source for vertical video styles. Keep the original uncropped so each format has room to reframe.

faq.q: Do the industry pages cover which ad format works for each platform?
faq.a: They point to the platform pages, where formats are matched to TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube Shorts, Amazon and Shopify. For example, vertical video fits in-feed placements, while square photos fit listings and most feed ads.

faq.q: How do I make sure the result looks like my actual product?
faq.a: Upload one photo with the product's shape, color and label area fully visible, and keep the scene description focused on that item. The generation keeps the product unchanged while placing it in the scene you choose.

steps.sourceHint: Keep the full bag, handle, and zipper visible.
steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. In a bright kitchen an adult places a packed lunch container inside the insulated bag, closes the zipper and lifts it by the handle to leave. Preserve the soft sage bag shape and color. Morning window light, candid lifestyle phone-video look. Medium follow framing with one smooth handheld move. End with the zipped lunch bag lifted by its handle. Sound: fabric rustle, zipper and quiet home ambience; no music.
